name: Argos
locality: Argos-Mykines Municipality; Commune of Argos; Argos Municipal Unit
text: Argos (; Greek: Άργος [ˈarɣos]; Ancient: Ἄργος [árɡos]) is a city and a former municipality in the Peloponnese region of Greece, and one of the oldest continuously inhabited cities in the world. It is the largest city in Argolis, having nearly twice the population of its capital, Nafplio. Since the 2011 local government reform it has been part of the municipality of Argos-Mykines, of which it is a municipal unit.

depictions.name: Argos
depictions.text: the builder of the Argo Argos, nicknamed the White City, is a city and a region in Argolis, a regional unit of the Peloponnese region of Greece. Among the oldest cities of Greece, it was a dominant and powerful polis during the Mycenaean period. Argos was founded between its two akropoleis and is home to many mythical heroes, though in the 5th century BCE its fame was based on the accomplishments of its talented sculptors.
